1.title: The OSI Model and Encapsulation
1.text: Welcome to Module one: The O S I Model and Encapsulation. It covers the exam area one point zero Networking Concepts. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. The seven layers. Encapsulation. Which layer is the problem? Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: one point zero Networking Concepts (twenty-three percent). Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Network plus N ten to nine exam objectives, version four point zero.

1.title: The seven layers
1.text: The seven layers. The O S I model is a reference model that splits network communication into seven layers. Each layer serves the layer above and uses the layer below.

1.title: The seven layers, continued
1.text: The seven layers. The figure shows this: The seven O S I layers with their data units and typical devices and protocols.

1.title: The seven layers, continued
1.text: The seven layers. seven. Layer: Application. Job: Network services for applications. Data unit: Data. Examples: H T T P, H T T P S, D N S, S M T P, S S H. six. Layer: Presentation. Job: Format, encrypt, compress data. Data unit: Data. Examples: T L S (often placed here), J P E G, encoding. five. Layer: Session. Job: Open, manage and close conversations. Data unit: Data. Examples: Net B I O S sessions, R P C. four. Layer: Transport. Job: End-to-end delivery, ports, reliability. Data unit: Segment (T C P) or datagram (U D P). Examples: T C P, U D P.

1.title: The seven layers, continued
1.text: The seven layers. three. Layer: Network. Job: Logical addressing and routing. Data unit: Packet. Examples: I P, I C M P, routers. two. Layer: Data link. Job: Local delivery with M A C addresses, error detection. Data unit: Frame. Examples: Ethernet, switches, M A C. one. Layer: Physical. Job: Bits on the medium (signals, cables, radio). Data unit: Bits. Examples: Cables, hubs, repeaters, N I Cs. Exam tip: Memory aid, top to bottom: "All People Seem To Need Data Processing"; bottom to top: "Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away". Know the data unit at each layer: bits, frames, packets, segments.

1.title: Encapsulation
1.text: Encapsulation. Data moves down the stack at the sender, each layer adding a header (encapsulation), and up the stack at the receiver, each layer removing its header (de-encapsulation). Transport. Port numbers (source and destination). Network. I P addresses. Data link. M A C addresses and a trailer with a frame check sequence.

1.title: Which layer is the problem?
1.text: Which layer is the problem? Hub, repeater, cable, N I C signaling. one. Switch, bridge, M A C addresses, V L A N tag. two. Router, I P address, I C M P. three. T C P, U D P, port numbers, stateful firewall (tracks sessions). four. Proxy, web application firewall, H T T P, D N S. seven. Exam tip: A "layer three switch" routes (layer three) as well as switches (layer two). A layer four load balancer decides by I P and port; a layer seven load balancer decides by U R L or content. Exam tip: Switches work at layer two and routers at layer three; when a scenario names an I P address, think layer three; a M A C address, think layer two.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A technician finds a duplicate M A C address on a switch. At which O S I layer is the problem? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Layer two, the data link layer. M A C addresses operate at the data link layer.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A router forwards a packet using the destination I P address. Which layer does this describe? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Layer three, the network layer. Routing uses logical I P addresses at layer three.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Which data unit is used at the transport layer for T C P? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Segment. T C P data units are segments (U D P uses datagrams).

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A cable has a broken wire and the link is down. Which layer does the fault belong to? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Layer one, the physical layer. Cables and signaling are layer one.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A load balancer chooses a server using the requested U R L. At which layer does it work? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Layer seven, the application layer. Choosing by U R L or content is layer seven behavior.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many layers does the O S I model have? Answer: Seven. Question two. Which layer uses M A C addresses? Answer: Layer two, the data link layer. Question three. Which layer provides end-to-end delivery and ports? Answer: Layer four, the transport layer.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the data unit at layer three? Answer: A packet. Question five. What is the data unit at layer two? Answer: A frame. Question six. What is encapsulation? Answer: Each layer adds its header as data moves down the stack at the sender.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Layer: Name Data unit Typical items. seven: Application Data H T T P, D N S, proxy. six: Presentation Data encryption, formats. five: Session Data session control. four: Transport Segment T C P, U D P, ports. three: Network Packet I P, router. two: Data link Frame M A C, switch. one: Physical Bits cables, hubs.
